title: Nine years off the stage after Pharoah
summary: McBee was unable to find work from about 1974 to 1983 and says it made him a better person.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah. Well let me wrap up with effusive thanks for your stories and your wisdom. And I wonder if you, you’ve had so many high points, have you had any regrets in your life or does that kind of thinking just not work for you?

Well you asked me in the previous talk whether or not I had bumps or periods that prevailed on my arrival in New York. Financially I never really suffered any drama of that. But I did enter a period of nine years, this was right after Pharoah Sanders that I was off the stage for nine years. There were social considerations that were beyond my control and I could not find a stage for nine years. So this was like from maybe ’74 through, what’s that, ’83, ’84 something like that. I was off the stage for that period of time. And given the development of my music personally, you know, although I stayed in the woodshed most of the time, I think that that impacted who I was, that I had to fast, recover from, in order to get myself back on track. Something that happened that I © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-

mentioned that we’re going through as a nation now. Life entered and caused me to stop. I was moving really fast and very successfully in New York so I had to stop and make an adjustment as to who I was and what the next step was. It was a natural phenomenon that caused me to just go to the mirror and look and discover who you really are, Cecil McBee, because from the moment I played with Jimmy “Cry Cry” all the way through New York, it was fast track. I had never taken consideration of any measurable distractions. So that’s what I entered. So I had to work through some personal considerations that were — I should say now — rather worthy of my time, because I became a better person, better musician, and a better man.
